     8	/-!
     9	# Functoriality of the WIDENED vehicle along an arbitrary test morphism (R2, residue (b))
    10	
    11	The widened vehicle `divFamZarAff` (`…AffVehicle.lean`) is functorial along an **arbitrary**
    12	morphism `f : T' ⟶ T` of test objects: the value of the restricted family at an affine open
    13	`W ⊆ T'.left` — whose `f`-image need not lie in any affine open of `T.left` — is *glued* over a
    14	finite basic-open refinement of `W` subordinate to the preimages of affine opens, using the
    15	widened S5b Zariski keystones through the basic-open toolkit (`…AffMapKit.lean`).
    16	
    17	This is the last packaging layer of R2 residue (b): with it the widened carrier of protection
    18	I-0492 is a functor on the whole slice over `Spec k`, which is the generality every DD-R
    19	consumer (`DivRepGlobalData.pull_comp`) is stated at.
    20	
    21	## Main declarations
    22	
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff.IsPullbackValue` — the characterizing property of the glued
    24	  value, with `pullbackValue_unique` (Zariski separation) and `exists_isPullbackValue`
    25	  (Zariski gluing).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAff.map C n f : divFamZarAff C n T → divFamZarAff C n T'`, with
    27	  `map_id`, `map_comp`, and the no-gluing evaluation `mapVal_eq_mapAlgHom`.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_naturality` — over affine tests, `map` along
    29	  `Spec` of an algebra map is `DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom` of that map under the widened affine
    30	  collapse.
    31	
    32	## What is and is not asserted
    33	
    34	Everything here is about the Zariski topology of the **base**.  R2 widened the curve side, so
    35	these are the chart-typed proofs of `DivisorFamilyZarMap.lean` with `DivFamZar` replaced by
    36	`DivFamZarAff` — no new geometry, and in particular **no `|P¹(k)|` hypothesis** anywhere in the
    37	statements or their route.  What the widened lane still owes is unchanged by this file: the
    38	subordinate Stacks 0B8B input (residue (a), out of scope per I-0492 clause 2).
    39	-/

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartLocalSurjectivity
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# At a one-point test, Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity
    10	
    11	DAT-J's `quasiCompact` field reduces — in either coordinate system, see
    12	`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean` and `Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean` — to one
    13	statement `hcl`: **every point of the representing object has its class pulled back along some
    14	field point of the divisor scheme**.  Both of those files record that `hcl` has no producer,
    15	and the routes they name (the Abel image, finite-separable descent) are the expensive ones.
    16	
    17	This file supplies the general fact that reprices the *first* half of that statement, and it
    18	is not about `pic⁰` at all:
    19	
    20	> a Zariski covering sieve of a scheme whose space is a `Subsingleton` **contains the
    21	> identity**, so a locally surjective morphism of presheaves of types is honestly surjective
    22	> on sections there.
    23	
    24	`Spec K` for a field `K` is such a scheme (`Unique (PrimeSpectrum K)` in mathlib), and the
    25	tests `hcl` quantifies over are exactly `overSpec k κ(y)`.  So on the `hcl` side, coverage —
    26	antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, which the seam **already assumes** — is not
    27	merely "locally" available at a field point: it gives a section on the nose, with no descent
    28	step and no Abel image.
    29	
    30	## Why the statement is about a `Subsingleton` space and not about fields
    31	
    32	The proof looks at the space only, and it goes through for an arbitrary presheaf of types on
    33	`Scheme`: take a cover refining the sieve (`exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology`), take
    34	the component over the unique point, observe its base map is epi *because the target has at
    35	most one point*, conclude it is an isomorphism (`IsOpenImmersion.isIso`), and use
    36	`Sieve.downward_closed` along its inverse.  Nothing here mentions `pic⁰`, the curve, the
    37	divisor scheme, or the sheaf condition.  Stated in that generality deliberately: it is the
    38	mirror image of `Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`'s
    39	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`, which refutes the `V = ⊥` endpoint by
    40	looking only at the *emptiness* of the space.  Empty spaces kill local surjectivity; one-point
    41	spaces make it free.  Both are facts about the site, not about the Picard functor.
    42	
    43	## What this does NOT do, stated because the temptation here is exactly the audited failure mode
    44	
    45	**It does not discharge `hcl`, and it does not discharge any antecedent.**  What it gives is a
    46	section of the Σ-sheaf over `Spec κ(y)` *in the image of the atlas*, i.e. an index `i` and a
    47	`κ(y)`-point of the `i`-th chart source.  `hcl` asks for a point of `divSchemeOver …` whose
    48	class is `pic0Map C q lam` for the **one fixed** class `lam`.  Two gaps remain and neither is
    49	touched here:
    50	
    51	* the chart source of `mixedParamChart` is `(V i : Scheme)`, an *open of* `(D i).left`, and the
    52	  chart index `i` produced is the one coverage happens to supply — so the point obtained lies in
    53	  a chart of the atlas, not in a single named divisor scheme;
    54	* `hcl`'s `lam` is fixed *before* `y` is quantified, whereas coverage's index varies with the
    55	  point.  Collapsing that quantifier order is the real content of `hcl`, and this file leaves
    56	  it open.
    57	
    58	So the honest reading is: **the "local" in DAT-B's local surjectivity costs nothing at the
    59	tests DAT-J quantifies over.**  That is a subtraction from `hcl`'s price, not a payment of it.
    60	
    61	## Main declarations
    62	
    63	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — a covering sieve of a
    64	  `Subsingleton`-space scheme contains an isomorphism.  The only geometric input.
    65	* `AlgebraicGeometry.id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology` — hence it contains the identity, i.e. it
    66	  is the top sieve on the nose.
    67	* `AlgebraicGeometry.app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton` — hence local
    68	  surjectivity of an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types is surjectivity on sections
    69	  there.
    70	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton` — the `pic⁰`
    71	  reading: at a one-point test, a covering chart family hits **every** section, by a genuine
    72	  index and a genuine point of that chart's source.
    73	-/
    74	
    75	set_option autoImplicit false
    76	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    77	
    78	universe u v
    79	
    80	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    81	
    82	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    83	
    84	/-! ## The site fact -/
    85	
    86	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains an isomorphism.**
    87	
    88	Take a cover refining the sieve; its component over the point `x` is an open immersion whose
    89	base map is surjective *because the target is a subsingleton*, hence an isomorphism.
    90	
    91	The `Subsingleton` hypothesis is on the space, and `x` witnesses that it is also nonempty —
    92	both are needed: on the empty scheme the bottom sieve covers
    93	(`Scheme.bot_mem_grothendieckTopology`) and contains no isomorphism at all. -/
    94	theorem exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
    95	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
    96	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ X), S.arrows g ∧ IsIso g := by
    97	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_grothendieckTopology hS
    98	  obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝒰.exists_eq x
    99	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (𝒰.f i) := 𝒰.map_prop i
   100	  haveI : Epi (𝒰.f i).base := by
   101	    rw [TopCat.epi_iff_surjective]
   102	    exact fun z => ⟨y, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩
   103	  exact ⟨𝒰.X i, 𝒰.f i, hle _ _ (Presieve.ofArrows.mk i), IsOpenImmersion.isIso (𝒰.f i)⟩
   104	
   105	/-- **A Zariski covering sieve of a scheme with at most one point contains the identity** —
   106	so on such a scheme "covering" carries no information beyond nonemptiness.
   107	
   108	`Sieve.downward_closed` along the inverse of the isomorphism above. -/
   109	theorem id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)]
   110	    (x : X) (S : Sieve X) (hS : S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology X) :
   111	    S.arrows (𝟙 X) := by
   112	  obtain ⟨Y, g, hg, hiso⟩ := exists_isIso_of_mem_zariskiTopology x S hS
   113	  have h := S.downward_closed hg (inv g)
   114	  rwa [IsIso.inv_hom_id] at h
   115	
   116	/-- **Zariski-local surjectivity IS surjectivity at a one-point test.**
   117	
   118	For an arbitrary morphism of presheaves of types on `Scheme`: the image sieve of a section is
   119	covering by hypothesis, hence contains the identity by the previous theorem, and an identity in
   120	the image sieve *is* a preimage of the section.
   121	
   122	No `pic⁰`, no curve, no sheaf condition — this is the counterpart of
   123	`not_isLocallySurjective_restrictChart_bot_of_presheaf`
   124	(`Picard/Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean`), which refutes local surjectivity on the *empty* space by
   125	the same kind of purely site-level argument. -/
   126	theorem app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton
   127	    {F G : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v} (φ : F ⟶ G)
   128	    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology φ]
   129	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (X : Type u)] (x : X) :
   130	    Function.Surjective (φ.app (op X)) := by
   131	  intro s
   132	  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ :=
   133	    id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology x _
   134	      (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem Scheme.zariskiTopology φ s)
   135	  exact ⟨t, by simpa using ht⟩
   136	
   137	/-! ## The instances at `Spec` of a field
   138	
   139	Recorded as `example`s rather than restated: both are mathlib instances
   140	(`PrimeSpectrum.instUnique` for a field), and the point of listing them is that the tests
   141	`hcl` quantifies over — `overSpec k κ(y)` — satisfy the hypotheses above with nothing to
   142	prove. -/
   143	
   144	section Field
   145	
   146	variable (K : Type u) [Field K]
   147	
   148	example : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   149	
   150	example : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of K) : Type u) := inferInstance
   151	
   152	end Field
   153	
   154	/-! ## The `pic⁰` reading -/
   155	
   156	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   157	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   158	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   159	
   160	/-- **At a one-point test, a covering chart family hits every section on the nose.**
   161	
   162	Given DAT-B's coverage (`ChartsCoverLocally`, the `pic⁰` spelling a producer actually attempts)
   163	and a test whose space has at most one point, every section `s` of the Σ-sheaf over that test
   164	is `f i` applied to a genuine point of the `i`-th chart source — no restriction to a
   165	neighbourhood, no refinement, no descent.
   166	
   167	This is what makes the "local" in B-5/B-6 free at the tests DAT-J's `hcl` quantifies over
   168	(`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean`).  It does **not** produce `hcl`: the index `i` here is
   169	whichever one coverage supplies at `s`, while `hcl` fixes one class `lam` on one divisor scheme
   170	before quantifying over points.  See this file's module docstring for the two surviving gaps. -/
   171	theorem exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton {ι : Type u}
   172	    {X : ι → Scheme.{u}} (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   173	    (hcov : ChartsCoverLocally C f)
   174	    {T : Scheme.{u}} [Subsingleton (T : Type u)] (t : T)
   175	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   176	    ∃ (i : ι) (x : T ⟶ X i), (f i).app (op T) x = s := by
   177	  have hid := id_mem_of_mem_zariskiTopology t _ (hcov T s)
   178	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hid
   179	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hid
   180	  exact ⟨i, x, by simpa using hx⟩
   181	
   182	end AlgebraicGeometry

     9	/-!
    10	# The fixed-ledger-parameter reduction reaches the coverage consumer
    11	
    12	## Current status (2026-07-30): this is no longer the route endpoint
    13	
    14	Every theorem below remains true, but the advertised `IsDivisorDegree C g` residue was created
    15	by fixing the chart parameter to the minimal ledger bound `M·δ + g`.  Coverage only needs a
    16	parameter *at least* that bound.  `Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.admissibleCoverageParameter`
    17	chooses a larger positive-theta-degree multiple, and
    18	`exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ` proves unconditionally that one resulting
    19	legal chart locus is all of every `pic⁰` test.  Read the reductions below as the exact cost of
    20	the fixed-parameter branch, not as an open hypothesis of DAT-B.
    21	
    22	`Picard/Pic0ChartIndexAdmissible.lean` reduces the chart layer's `hdeg` binder to
    23	`IsDivisorDegree C c` ("`c` is the degree of some divisor on `C_k`").  That is a statement about
    24	a group homomorphism's image, with no chart in it.  A reduction that no consumer can consume is
    25	worth nothing, though (`I-1345`'s own lesson: price the *consumer's* carrier), so this file
    26	plugs it in at the one place the tree actually needs it.
    27	
    28	`exists_chartIndex_mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex` (`Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.lean:349`) takes
    29	the constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − (M·δ + g)` as a hypothesis, and its docstring says so
    30	explicitly: *"`Z` of prescribed degree is a divisor-side existence statement this file does not
    31	prove and does not claim."*  `mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex_of_isDegree` below discharges
    32	exactly that clause from `IsDivisorDegree`, with the twist exponent chosen for us (`m = 0`).
    33	
    34	## What this buys, stated exactly
    35	
    36	Coverage's locus membership at the fixed ledger parameter rests on **one arithmetic hypothesis**
    37	about the base field — `IsDivisorDegree C (M·δ + g)` — in place of an unexhibited pair `(m, Z)`.
    38	The splitting/degree-zero inputs are unchanged, and the following are **untouched**: antecedent 1
    39	(`IsChartUniv`), the pointwise-to-neighbourhood spreading-out that `Pic0ChartCoverageSlice.lean`
    40	records as absent, and `rep` at any parameter.  **No antecedent of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`
    41	is discharged here.**
    42	
    43	## And what the remaining hypothesis costs, honestly
    44	
    45	`IsDivisorDegree C (M·δ + g)` is **not** known to hold.  Over an arbitrary base field `deg_k` is
    46	weighted by residue degrees, so its image is a proper subgroup of `ℤ` in general; the multiples
    47	of `d₁` are admissible unconditionally (`isDegree_mul_thetaDeg`) and `M·δ + g` is not visibly
    48	one of them.
    49	
    50	But the residue is **smaller than that paragraph suggests**, and `isDegree_mul_thetaDeg_add_iff`
    51	is why: if `M·δ` is a multiple of `d₁`, then `IsDivisorDegree C (M·δ + g)` is *equivalent* to
    52	`IsDivisorDegree C g` — the ledger constants drop out entirely and what remains is whether the
    53	**genus** is a divisor degree.  So the open question is one hypothesis about `π` versus
    54	`thetaP1 C` (are their fibre degrees commensurable?) plus one about the curve at `g`.
    55	
    56	**And the "if" costs nothing** (`isDegree_ledger_add_iff`): read on `C.left`, `δ = windowδ π` *is*
    57	the degree of a divisor — the fibre divisor of the ledger's own `π` — so `M` copies of it shift
    58	the target by `M·δ` in both directions, with no hypothesis.
    59	
    60	So the residue of the fixed-ledger-parameter branch is exactly one question:
    61	
    62	> **is the genus `g` the degree of a divisor on `C.left`?**
    63	
    64	No ledger constant, no θ-class, no chart, no second map.  It is still open — `deg_k` is
    65	residue-degree weighted, so nothing forces `g` into its image over an arbitrary base field, and
    66	the tree's only residue-degree-one point needs `[IsSepClosed k]`
    67	(`Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints`, `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean:278`), which the
    68	arbitrary-field statement forbids assuming.
    69	
    70	**Two earlier versions of this paragraph priced that residue higher, and both were refuted** —
    71	first "two maps on two different curves, unrelated in the tree", then "a commensurability question
    72	between `π` and `thetaP1 C`".  Each was measured, each was wrong in the expensive direction, and
    73	each is recorded at the theorem that refuted it (`isDivisorDegree_iff_left`,
    74	`isDegree_ledger_add_iff`).  The `rfl` fact `windowδ (thetaP1 C) = classDeg k (thetaCechClass C)`
    75	survives from the first round and is what `isDegree_mul_thetaDeg_add_iff` rests on.
    76	
    77	## The chart index this route produces is UNIFORM in the point — read against `I-1389`
    78	
    79	`I-1389` warns that a coverage statement at a *fixed* chart index is strictly stronger than
    80	DAT-B's antecedent 2, because the heterogeneous-atlas apparatus (`mixedParamChart`, the
    81	index-by-`m` atlas of `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack`) exists precisely so different points may use
    82	different charts.  The warning applies to this file, so the position is stated rather than left
    83	for a reader to work out:
    84	
    85	* the `(m, Z)` comes from `hadm`, which **does not mention the point** `t`, so the chart index
    86	  really is uniform in `t`.  **But that is a fact about the proof, not about the statement** —
    87	  `mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex_of_isDegree` puts its `∃ m Z` *inside* the per-point binders, so
    88	  read literally it is the non-uniform claim.  A first draft asserted the uniformity only in this
    89	  paragraph; since `I-1389`'s whole point is that a chart-index claim must say which of the two it
    90	  is, the uniform form is now a theorem —
    91	  `exists_uniform_chartIndex_forall_mem_chartLocus_of_isDegree`, with `∃ m Z` hoisted outside
    92	  every binder.  (Found by a fresh-context audit of this file.)
    93	* it is nonetheless **not** one-chart coverage in `I-1389`'s sense and does not imply it: even in
    94	  the hoisted form the splitting data `L`, `M₀`, `hM₀` stays quantified per point *inside* the
    95	  conclusion.  What is uniform is the chart index alone.
    96	
    97	For this historical branch, the non-uniformity is in the **splitting data**, not in the chart
    98	parameter.  The newer admissible-parameter endpoint eliminates that splitting input internally
    99	and hoists the chart index across every test and class.  Neither result produces the remaining
   100	neighbourhood morphism into the chart.
   101	
   102	## Main declarations
   103	
   104	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex_of_isDegree` — locus membership at the ledger
   105	  parameter from `IsDivisorDegree`, replacing the unexhibited `(m, Z)`.  This is *already* the
   106	  `∃`-form DAT-B B-6 packages; the last section records why a second declaration a first draft
   107	  added was the same proposition and was removed.
   108	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_uniform_chartIndex_forall_mem_chartLocus_of_isDegree` — the same, with
   109	  the chart index hoisted out of every per-point binder, so the uniformity is in the statement.
   110	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDivisorDegree_iff_left` — the predicate transports to `C.left`; the
   111	  base-changed curve is not a second curve.
   112	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isDegree_ledger_add_iff` — the ledger constants drop out unconditionally.
   113	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_chartLocus_of_ledgerIndex_of_isDegree_genus` — the fixed-parameter
   114	  endpoint: locus membership at the ledger parameter from `IsDivisorDegree C g`; superseded as
   115	  the live route by `exists_uniform_admissibleCoverageChart_eq_univ`.
   116	-/
   117	
   118	set_option autoImplicit false
   119	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/

   103	/-- **A slice morphism IS a bare morphism plus the Σ-equation** — the refutation of this
   104	file's original "the Σ-component is absorbed for free" claim, stated so it cannot be re-made.
   105	
   106	Both directions are `rfl`: `Over.homMk` bundles `(x, hx)` into `g` with `g.left = x`, and
   107	`Over.w` projects it back out.  So working in the slice **moves** the Σ-equation into the input
   108	type; it does not discharge it, and a producer owes exactly what it owed before.  What changes
   109	is only that the equation stops appearing as a goal — which is why the original claim looked
   110	measured.
   111	
   112	The general form of this check (inbox `I-1024`): when a file reports an obligation absorbed by
   113	a richer input type, derive the new hypothesis from the old one.  One probe settles it. -/
   114	theorem slice_iff_bare {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   115	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens) :
   116	    Nonempty (Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D) ↔
   117	      ∃ x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ D.left, x ≫ D.hom = W.ι ≫ s.1 :=
   118	  ⟨fun ⟨g⟩ => ⟨g.left, Over.w g⟩, fun ⟨x, hx⟩ => ⟨Over.homMk x hx⟩⟩
   119	
   120	/-! ## The reduction: one class equation is the whole datum -/
   121	
   122	/-- **THE DATUM FROM A SLICE MORPHISM PLUS ONE CLASS EQUATION.**
   123	
   124	The hypothesis `hcl` is the class equation in the slice over `Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1)`: the chart
   125	value of the divisor family that `g` names is the given class, restricted.  Given it, the full
   126	pair equation that `chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` consumes holds — the Σ-component is
   127	`Over.w g` and the `Over.mkCongr` transport is handled by `Over.sigmaExtension_ext`.
   128	
   129	This is the discount `abelChartApp_eq`'s header asks a producer to pay and a producer of this
   130	shape does not owe. -/
   131	theorem datum_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   132	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   133	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   134	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   135	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   136	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens)
   137	    (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D)
   138	    (hcl : (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
   139	        ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   140	          (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
   141	      = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
   142	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
   143	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩) :
   144	    (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) g.left
   145	      = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s := by
   146	  rw [abelChartApp_eq]
   147	  rw [show ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s)
   148	      = ⟨W.ι ≫ s.1, (pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   149	          (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2⟩ from rfl]
   150	  exact Over.sigmaExtension_ext (pic0TypeFunctor C) (Over.w g) hcl
   151	
   152	/-- **The converse of `datum_of_slice`**, so the pair is visibly an equivalence and this file
   153	claims no reduction (the `I-0896` criterion).  From the datum equation the class equation is
   154	read off by `Over.sigmaExtension_snd_eq`, the same one-liner with the projection replacing the
   155	constructor. -/
   156	theorem bare_of_slice {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   157	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   158	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   159	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   160	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   161	    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (W : Y.Opens)
   162	    (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D)
   163	    (hdatum : (abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) g.left
   164	      = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   165	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
   166	        ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   167	          (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
   168	      = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
   169	          (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
   170	        chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩ :=
   171	  Over.sigmaExtension_snd_eq (pic0TypeFunctor C) (Over.w g) hdatum
   172	
   173	/-! ## Through to antecedent 2
   174	
   175	The two composites, so the discount lands at the seam rather than in mid-air.  Both are
   176	stated for the ONE-CHART family `fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart …`: the slice reduction is about
   177	the chart application, which does not see the index, and heterogeneity is orthogonal
   178	(`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`). -/
   179	
   180	variable (C π n) in
   181	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` from per-point slice data over affine tests.**
   182	
   183	The hypothesis is the coverage obligation in its cheapest measured form: over an affine test
   184	only (`Pic0ChartCoverageAffineTest.lean`), a slice morphism rather than a bare morphism (so
   185	the Σ-component is `Over.w`), and one class equation.  Nothing else stands between it and the
   186	sieve condition. -/
   187	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_slice {ι : Type u} [Nonempty ι] {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   188	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   189	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   190	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   191	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   192	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
   193	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D),
   194	        (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
   195	            ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   196	              (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
   197	          = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
   198	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
   199	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩) :
   200	    ChartsCoverLocally C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg) := by
   201	  refine chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal C _ fun Y _ s y => ?_
   202	  obtain ⟨W, hyW, g, hcl⟩ := h Y s y
   203	  exact ⟨W, hyW, Classical.arbitrary ι, g.left,
   204	    datum_of_slice rep m Z hdeg Y s W g hcl⟩
   205	
   206	variable (C π n) in
   207	/-- **Antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, from slice data over affine tests.**
   208	
   209	The composite with B-6 (`isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`).  This is the honest endpoint of the
   210	reduction: the instance the DAT-glue seam consumes, from the cheapest form of the coverage
   211	datum the tree can currently state.
   212	
   213	**The class equation is still open**, and it is the whole of what is left here.  Its cost is a
   214	divisor family over a *neighbourhood* produced from data at a *point* — a spreading-out, absent
   215	from the tree for this carrier. -/
   216	theorem isLocallySurjective_of_slice {ι : Type u} [Nonempty ι] {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   217	    (rep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   218	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   219	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   220	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   221	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
   222	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (g : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ D),
   223	        (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr (Over.w g)).op
   224	            ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   225	              (Over.homMk W.ι rfl : Over.mk (W.ι ≫ s.1) ⟶ Over.mk s.1).op s.2)
   226	          = ⟨chartValue C π n m Z (Over.mk (g.left ≫ D.hom))
   227	              (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl)),
   228	            chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg _ _⟩) :
   229	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
   230	      (Sigma.desc (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChart C π n rep m Z hdeg)) :=
   231	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc _ (chartsCoverLocally_of_slice C π n rep m Z hdeg h)
   232	
   233	end
   234	
   235	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# B-5, the fibre step: the greedy drop RUN at the splitting field, as a `chartLocus` witness
    12	
    13	**Title corrected (issue I-0615): this file is steps 4 and 5, not "4–6".**  Step 6 — feeding the
    14	drop's output `Σ` back as the chart index — is NOT here and is not discharged anywhere; see the
    15	DEFECT section of `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`, which explains why the drop stage and the
    16	index stage carry different `Z`.  The original "4–6" wording is what that retraction corrects.
    17	
    18	`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5 happen entirely on the curve over the splitting field `L`.  This file
    19	runs them and hands the result to `Picard/Pic0ChartTwistSplit.lean`'s introduction rule, so
    20	that what comes out is membership of `chartLocus`.
    21	
    22	## The statement, and what is a hypothesis rather than a construction
    23	
    24	`exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` takes:
    25	
    26	* the presentation of the *twisted* fibre class over `L` by a Čech class `M`
    27	  (`hM` — supplied at step 1 by `picEtAffineEquiv_map_chartTwistFactor_eq_unit`);
    28	* a divisor `W₀` in that class with vanishing `H¹` and degree `g + e`
    29	  (`hdeg`/`h1` — supplied at step 4: the class's degree is computed by
    30	  `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegree.lean`, and the vanishing comes from the fibre's OWN
    31	  vanishing bound, which is where step 3's per-fibre `m` is spent);
    32	* the admissible point oracle at `L` (`hdense`/`hPcl`/`hPdeg` — supplied at step 5 by
    33	  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at the base-changed `K_s`-points).
    34	
    35	and produces an `S ≥ 0` of degree `e`, supported in the oracle, with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`,
    36	`h¹ = 0`, together with `IsSplitWitness` at the twisted class.
    37	
    38	**What is deliberately a hypothesis:** the *existence* of `W₀` of the right degree with
    39	`h¹ = 0`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and per `w4-datb` §0.2.2 (the I-0204 discipline)
    40	its bound `b_L` is a **per-fibre** constant that provably does not transport from `k` — so it
    41	must be chosen at `L`, inside the coverage proof, against `L`'s own instance.  Threading it as
    42	a hypothesis here keeps that choice visible instead of burying it: a caller who cannot produce
    43	`W₀` has not yet done step 3.
    44	
    45	**Why the `h⁰ = 1` conclusion is carried even though `IsSplitWitness` does not ask for it:**
    46	the witness predicate asks only for vanishing `H¹` (documented at `IsSplitWitness`; the
    47	worksheets' "effective degree-`g` witness with `h¹ = 0`" is stronger than what the tree's
    48	predicates state).  But `h⁰ = 1` is what DAT-C's normalization and GAP-2's uniqueness need, and
    49	it is free here — the drop produces it.  Dropping it from the conclusion would force a later
    50	lane to re-run the induction.
    51	
    52	## Main declarations
    53	
    54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop` — **the fibre step of B-5**: the greedy drop
    55	  at `L`, packaged as `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class plus the `h⁰ = 1` normalization.
    56	-/
    57	
    58	set_option autoImplicit false
    59	/- Statements mix `relCurve C L` with the product spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`. -/
    60	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    61	/- `lake env lean` drops the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` (I-0161). -/
    62	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    64	universe u

    67	open TopologicalSpace Opposite

    69	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    71	open AlgebraicJacobian

    73	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    74	
    75	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    76	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    77	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    78	
    79	noncomputable section
    80	
    81	/-! ## The fibre step -/
    82	
    83	variable (C) in
    84	/-- **B-5's fibre step** (`w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–5, run at the splitting field; **not** step 6 —
    85	see the header correction and issue I-0615).
    86	
    87	Given the twisted fibre class presented over `L` by `M`, a divisor `W₀` in `M` of degree
    88	`g + e` with vanishing `H¹`, and an admissible point oracle `P` on the `L`-curve, the greedy
    89	drop produces `S` of degree `e` supported in `P` with `h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1` and `h¹(W₀ − S) = 0`;
    90	and the class of `W₀` itself already certifies `IsSplitWitness` of the twisted class.
    91	
    92	The two conclusions serve different consumers, which is why both are returned: the
    93	`IsSplitWitness` half is `chartLocus` membership (`w4-datb` §1.2's target), while the
    94	`h⁰ = 1` half is what DAT-C's normalization and the GAP-2 uniqueness of the effective
    95	representative consume.
    96	
    97	**The `S`-becomes-the-chart-index sentence that stood here is RETRACTED** (issue I-0615, and this
    98	was its last residual site — the file header at the top of this module already carried the
    99	correction, and the worksheet's `w4-datb` §1.2 SECOND AMENDMENT retracts it harder).  Coverage does
   100	not feed `S` back as the chart index, because it does not need the drop at all:
   101	`IsSplitWitness` asks for `h¹ = 0` and for **neither** effectivity **nor** degree `g`
   102	(`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`, `mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1`).  What the drop's output
   103	*is* needed for is DAT-C's canonical section and GAP-2's uniqueness, which do require `0 ≤ W` and
   104	`h⁰ = 1` — i.e. the chart map's injectivity, not its coverage. -/
   105	theorem exists_isSplitWitness_of_drop {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
   106	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k K)) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   107	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra K L] [IsScalarTower k K L]
   108	    [Module.Finite K L] [Algebra.IsSeparable K L]
   109	    (g e : ℕ) (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   110	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   111	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L (picEtAffineEquiv C K μ)
   112	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
   113	    (W₀ : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor)
   114	    (hW₀ : Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W₀
   115	      = M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
   116	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W₀ = (g : ℤ) + e)
   117	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L W₀) 1))
   118	    (P : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
   119	    (hdense : ∀ U : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).Opens,
   120	      (U : Set ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
   121	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
   122	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L x = 1) :
   123	    IsSplitWitness C (μ * thetaFamily C (chartTwistClass C m Z) (overSpec k K))
   124	      ∧ ∃ S : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧
   125	        Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   126	        (∀ (x : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left))
   127	          (hx : x ≠ genericPoint ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left)),
   128	          coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   129	        Sheaf.h0 ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) = 1 ∧
   130	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   131	          ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L (W₀ - S)) 1) := by
   132	  refine ⟨isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1, ?_⟩
   133	  -- the χ-value at the fibre field, transported from `k` (genus is base-field invariant)
   134	  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
   135	  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so `chi_relCurve_baseField`'s
   136	  -- `relCurve`-spelled binders do not synthesise without these three re-keyings.
   137	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   138	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   139	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   140	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   141	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   142	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   143	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   144	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   145	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   146	  have hχL : Sheaf.chi ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) = 1 - (g : ℤ) :=
   147	    chi_relCurve_baseField C L g hχ
   148	  exact exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (K := L) g hχL P hdense hPcl hPdeg W₀ e hdeg h1
   149

    10	/-!
    11	# The per-point field-point statement of DAT-J is FREE from DAT-B coverage
    12	
    13	`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean` and `Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean` reduce DAT-J's
    14	`quasiCompact` field to `hcl`, and both record that it has **no producer of any shape**.  The
    15	routes they name are the Abel image and finite-separable descent.
    16	
    17	This file measures that pricing and finds the *per-point* half of it free.  Two results, and the
    18	second is the one that reprices the row:
    19	
    20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0Map_lamOfDivRep` — the **class-coordinate bridge**: restricting
    21	  `lamOfDivRep` (`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean`) along any test morphism `q : T ⟶ D` gives
    22	  the *chart value* of the `D`-point `q`.  Pure naturality — `chartValueTrans`'s own naturality
    23	  plus `RepresentableBy.homEquiv_comp` at `q ≫ 𝟙`.  So the class `hcl` speaks about is, at every
    24	  test, the chart value; nothing in `hcl` is about a class one still has to construct.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_chart_field_point_of_chartsCoverLocally` — **the per-point statement,
    26	  discharged from coverage alone**: given DAT-B coverage for a chart family and *any* Σ-sheaf
    27	  section over the field point of `y`, there is an index and an honest `Spec κ(y)`-point of that
    28	  chart's source whose chart value **is** that section.  No descent, no Abel image, no refinement
    29	  to a neighbourhood.  The section may be the one the representation names for `y`
    30	  (`section_of_rep_at_field_point` below), which is what makes this bear on `hcl`.
    31	
    32	The engine is `app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton`
    33	(`Picard/Pic0ChartFieldTestSurjective.lean`): at a one-point test, Zariski-local surjectivity
    34	*is* surjectivity, so the "local" in B-5/B-6 costs nothing at exactly the tests `hcl`
    35	quantifies over.
    36	
    37	## What is NOT discharged — read this before quoting the file
    38	
    39	**`hcl` is not proved here, and no antecedent of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` is discharged.**
    40	The results above are implications whose antecedent is DAT-B coverage, which has no producer at
    41	any `V` (`Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean`, `Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean` for the `⊥` end).  Trading an
    42	unproduced hypothesis for another unproduced hypothesis is not progress, and this file does not
    43	claim it is.  What it claims is narrower and checkable: **given coverage, the per-point half of
    44	`hcl` costs nothing**, so a lane pricing DAT-J should not schedule it as separate work.
    45	
    46	**THE GAP LIST BELOW WAS WRONG TWICE, BOTH TIMES IN MY OWN FAVOUR** — found by a fresh-context
    47	adversarial audit of this file and reproduced by me before accepting (`I-1434`, `I-1436`; lesson
    48	`I-1437`: a gap list written as the honest-ledger section reads as already-audited, so nobody
    49	probes it).  The original list had three items; item 1 was smaller than stated and item 3 had
    50	been closed fifteen minutes before this file landed.  Corrected list:
    51	
    52	1. **ONE Σ-TRANSPORT, not a carrier mismatch.**  The original text said the point produced lands
    53	   in `(V i : Scheme)`, "an *open of* `(D i).left`", while `hcl` wants a point of the divisor
    54	   scheme.  That clause is **idle**: `restrictChart` *is* `yoneda.map V.ι ≫ f`, so composing the

    56	   `(congrArg Sigma.fst hx).trans (Over.testPoint y).w` gives an honest `⟶ D i` — measured, it
    57	   elaborates.  What genuinely remains is the Σ *second* component: `Over.sigmaExtension_snd_eq`
    58	   leaves `(pic0TypeFunctor C).map (Over.mkCongr hfst).op`, and `mkCongr hfst` is not `rfl`-provably
    59	   the identity.  `Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff` (`Picard/OverSigmaExtension.lean`) is the
    60	   seam built for exactly this.  So: **one transport lemma**, named, not a carrier problem.
    61	2. **The index varies with the point.**  This item stands, and it is the one real residue.  See
    62	   `Picard/JacobianDataQcFiniteFamily.lean`, which moves the qc field's index quantifier inside
    63	   for exactly this reason, and ajcr-p4's `I-1389`, which shows a *fixed*-index coverage

    65	   family of answering carriers finite, and coverage supplies no bound on how many indices the
    66	   points of `J` use.

    68	   ajcr-p3's `I-1391` for the negative half (`CompactSpace` of an open does not follow by
    69	   instance resolution — true) and missed the *positive* half from that lane's same commit:
    70	   `compactSpace_isOpen_divSchemeOver` (`Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactNoetherian.lean`) proves
    71	   `CompactSpace (V : Scheme)` for **every** open of `divSchemeOver`, which is exactly the chart
    72	   sources.  Verified by `#check`.

    75	producer of any shape" is, at HEAD, false as an unqualified sentence:
    76	`quasiCompact_jacobianDataOfFiniteMixedParamCharts` (`Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactNoetherian.lean`)

    80	(class-indexed) atlas, which is the one the tree plans to build.  Read every "no producer"
    81	sentence in this file and in `Picard/JacobianDataQcFiniteFamily.lean` with that qualifier.

    83	So the corrected ledger: DAT-J's qc field, **at an infinite atlas**, owed one statement.  Its
    84	per-point half is free given coverage; what remains owed is one named Σ-transport and the index
    85	quantifier.  Not a geometric input either way — a repricing in the cheap direction, twice over.

   104	/-! ## The class-coordinate bridge -/
   105	
   106	/-- **`lamOfDivRep` restricted along a test morphism IS the chart value there.**
   107	
   108	`lamOfDivRep n divRep m Z hdeg` is the universal element of `divRep` pushed through
   109	`chartValueTrans` (`Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean`).  Restricting it along `q : T ⟶ D` gives
   110	the chart value of the `D`-point `q` — two naturality steps and nothing else:
   111	`picEtMap_chartValue` moves the restriction inside `chartValue`, and
   112	`RepresentableBy.homEquiv_comp` at `q ≫ 𝟙 D` identifies the restricted universal element with
   113	`divRep.homEquiv q`.
   114	
   115	**Why it matters for `hcl`.**  `hcl`'s equation is `pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (testPoint y)`
   116	with `lam` a class a producer must supply.  At `lam := lamOfDivRep …` — the class the chart layer
   117	already carries, per that file's own "`lam` is PRODUCED, not assumed" section — the left side is
   118	*the chart value of `q`*.  So `hcl` at that `lam` says exactly: **the class of `y` is a chart
   119	value at some field point**, with no reference to an Abel morphism or a compatibility square. -/
   120	theorem pic0Map_lamOfDivRep {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   121	    (divRep : (divFunctor C π n).RepresentableBy D)
   122	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   123	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
   124	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ))
   125	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ D) :
   126	    ((pic0Map C q (lamOfDivRep n divRep m Z hdeg)).1 : picEt C T)
   127	      = chartValue C π n m Z T (divRep.homEquiv q) := by
   128	  rw [pic0Map_coe, lamOfDivRep, chartValueTrans_app_coe, picEtMap_chartValue]
   129	  refine congrArg (chartValue C π n m Z T) ?_
   130	  have h := divRep.homEquiv_comp q (𝟙 D)
   131	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
   132	  exact h.symm
   133	
   134	/-! ## The section a representation names at a field point -/
   135	
   136	variable (C) in
   137	/-- **The Σ-sheaf section named by a point of a representing object.**
   138	
   139	For `prep` a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by `J` and `y : J.left`, the field point
   140	`Over.testPoint y` composed into the Σ-extension of `prep` is a section of the Σ-sheaf over
   141	`Spec κ(y)`.  Available from `prep` alone — no divisor data, no chart, no coverage.
   142	
   143	This is the section the next theorem is applied to, and the reason `hcl` is a statement about
   144	coverage rather than about constructing a class. -/
   145	def sectionOfRepAtFieldPoint {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   146	    (prep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J) (y : J.left) :
   147	    (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op ((overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left)) :=
   148	  (prep.toSigmaExtension).app
   149	    (op ((overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left)) (Over.testPoint y).left
   150	
   151	/-! ## The per-point statement, from coverage -/
   152	
   153	variable (C) in
   154	/-- **DAT-J's per-point field-point statement is free given DAT-B coverage.**
   155	
   156	Given a chart family that covers Zariski-locally, and any section `s` of the Σ-sheaf over the
   157	field point of `y`, there is an index `i` and a genuine morphism `Spec κ(y) ⟶ X i` whose chart
   158	value is `s` **on the nose** — no restriction to a neighbourhood, no refinement, no finite
   159	separable descent.
   160	
   161	The whole content is `app_surjective_of_isLocallySurjective_of_subsingleton`
   162	(`Picard/Pic0ChartFieldTestSurjective.lean`): `Spec κ(y)` has one point, and there local
   163	surjectivity is surjectivity.  Applied at `s := sectionOfRepAtFieldPoint C prep y` this is the
   164	per-point half of `hcl`, at the chart carriers.
   165	
   166	**Antecedent open.**  `ChartsCoverLocally` is antecedent 2 of `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` and
   167	has no producer at any `V`; this is an implication, not a discharge.  See the module docstring
   168	for the three surviving gaps between this and `hcl` as `JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean` states it —
   169	the carrier, the index quantifier, and compactness of the chart sources. -/
   170	theorem exists_chart_field_point_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   171	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   172	    (hcov : ChartsCoverLocally C f)
   173	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (y : T.left)
   174	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op ((overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left))) :
   175	    ∃ (i : ι) (x : (overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left ⟶ X i),
   176	      (f i).app (op ((overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left)) x = s :=
   177	  exists_chart_section_of_chartsCoverLocally_of_subsingleton f hcov
   178	    (Nonempty.some inferInstance) s
   179	
   180	variable (C π) in
   181	/-- **The same statement at the mixed-parameter atlas and the atlas's own class.**
   182	
   183	The form a DAT-J producer reads: for every point `y` of a `Pic⁰`-representing object, coverage
   184	supplies an index and a `Spec κ(y)`-point of the `i`-th chart source carrying the class of `y`.
   185	
   186	Stated separately because the mixed-parameter atlas is the family the tree plans to build, and
   187	because its chart sources `(V i : Scheme)` are the carriers the three gaps of the module
   188	docstring are about. -/
   189	theorem exists_mixedParamChart_field_point {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
   190	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
   191	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
   192	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   193	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   194	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
   195	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens)
   196	    (hcov : ChartsCoverLocally C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V))
   197	    {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} (prep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J) (y : J.left) :
   198	    ∃ (i : ι) (x : (overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left ⟶ ((V i : Scheme.{u}))),
   199	      (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V i).app
   200	          (op ((overSpec k (Over.testPointField y)).left)) x
   201	        = sectionOfRepAtFieldPoint C prep y :=
   202	  exists_chart_field_point_of_chartsCoverLocally C
   203	    (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) hcov y _

     8	/-!
     9	# B-5 assembly: from the fibre step to `chartLocus` membership over a GENERAL test
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean` runs `w4-datb` §1.2 steps 4–6 at a splitting field and
    12	produces `IsSplitWitness` of a twisted class over `overSpec k L`.  The coverage theorem
    13	(§1.2's `pic0_chartLocus_cover`) is a statement about a point `t` of a **general test** `T`:
    14	
    15	```
    16	∃ c : ChartIndex C, t ∈ chartLocus c lam
    17	```
    18	
    19	This file closes the gap between the two, which is one substitution and one collapse:
    20	
    21	* the fibre class at `t` is `picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam`, a class over the field
    22	  `κ(t)` — so the fibre step applies at `K := κ(t)` with no change;
    23	* `chartLocus` is *defined* as the split-witness predicate of the twisted class at that field
    24	  point, and the twist commutes with restriction (`picEtMap_chartTwist`), so
    25	  "`IsSplitWitness` of the twisted fibre class" **is** membership, by `Iff.rfl`.
    26	
    27	The second point is worth stating as a lemma rather than inlining: `chartTwist` is applied to
    28	`lam` over `T` and then restricted, whereas the fibre step produces the twist of the
    29	*restricted* class over `κ(t)`.  Those are equal, but not syntactically — `picEtMap_chartTwist`
    30	is the law, and `mem_chartLocus_of_isSplitWitness_fibre` is the resulting membership rule.
    31	
    32	## What remains of B-5 after this file
    33	
    34	**Twice corrected; read the DEFECT section for the full history.**  This header first said the
    35	only residues were the two per-fibre choices; a degree probe added a third (step 6's feedback);
    36	and on 2026-07-28 that third was **removed again** — not by discharging it but by showing
    37	coverage needs no drop, hence no feedback (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageNoDrop.lean`).  Step 2 is
    38	likewise landed now (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageDegreeStep2.lean`).
    39	
    40	The two per-fibre choices, which are residues *of the route through this file*:
    41	
    42	* **step 3, the twist exponent `m`.**  Chosen against the fibre's OWN DAT-0a bound `b_L`.  No
    43	  uniform `m₀` exists (§0.2.2, I-0204), so this is a genuine `∃ m` produced inside the
    44	  coverage proof, at the fibre.
    45	* **step 5's oracle instantiation.**  `Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`'s density keystone at
    46	  `P :=` the base-changed `K_s`-points, whose `residueDeg = 1` comes from
    47	  `rationalPointBaseChange_snd`.
    48	
    49	Both are `L`-level statements; neither is `divRep`- or certificate-gated.  Everything between

    57	  hypotheses, at `K := κ(t)`, give `t ∈ chartLocus`.
    58	-/

   106	/-! ## A DEFECT IN THIS FILE'S OWN COMPOSITION CLAIM — read before using `mem_chartLocus_of_drop`
   107	
   108	Found by a degree probe on this file, the same session it was written, and stated here rather
   109	than quietly repaired because the theorems below are **true and correctly proved** — what was
   110	wrong is the account of how they compose.
   111	
   112	**The arithmetic.** `hW₀` puts `W₀` in the class `M₀ · (twist class at Z)`.  For a degree-zero
   113	`λ` the presenting class `M₀` has `classDeg = 0`, so
   114	
   115	  `deg W₀ = m·d₁ − deg_k Z`,
   116	
   117	and `hdeg` demands `deg W₀ = g + e`.  Under the chart-index constraint `deg_k Z = m·d₁ − g`
   118	those force **`e = 0`**: the drop budget is zero and the greedy drop does nothing.  (Verified by
   119	deriving `(e : ℤ) = 0` from exactly this hypothesis pack.)
   120	
   121	**What that means.** The pack is *satisfiable* — it instantiates, and at `e = 0` the theorem is

   125	* the drop runs on `λ·θᵐ` — i.e. at `Z := 0`, where `chartTwistClass C m 0 = θᵐ` and the degree
   126	  is `m·d₁`, so the budget is `e = m·d₁ − g`, nonzero for the `m` step 3 chooses;
   127	* its **output** `Σ` is then the chart index's `Z`, at which the twisted class has degree `g`.

   163	/-- **THE B-5 ASSEMBLY** (`w4-datb` §1.2, everything except the two per-fibre choices).

   201	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   202	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]

events.text: The source confirms the hard step is genuinely absent, and it also exposes a mathematical warning: the fibre witness is allowed only after a finite separable residue-field extension. Such a point spreads étale-locally in general, not Zariski-locally. Before building a large spreading API around a false target, I’m auditing the existing one-chart and multi-chart no-go theorems to determine whether the roadmap’s Zariski neighborhood statement is itself unfaithful.

1	/-

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# The `V`-interval at a MULTI-INDEX atlas: the hypothesis the one-chart no-go was hiding
    10	
    11	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean` proves that coverage at a proper open `V ≠ ⊤` forces
    12	the chart map to be non-injective on some test, and `Picard/Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean`
    13	refutes both endpoints of the `V`-interval.  **Every one of those statements is about a
    14	one-chart atlas** (`ι := PUnit`), and the first file says so twice in its own limits section:
    15	
    16	> the dichotomy above is for a one-chart atlas … and **not** for `mixedParamChart` at
    17	> arbitrary `ι`.  The multi-index case is open and is *not* claimed here.
    18	
    19	The reason it gives is correct: coverage returns *some* index `i`, not the index `i₀` whose
    20	tautological section was tested, and if `i ≠ i₀` the two chart values live on different sources,
    21	so no non-injectivity of a single map follows.
    22	
    23	But the seam consumes `mixedParamChart` at arbitrary `ι`
    24	(`pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre`, `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibre.lean:259`).  So as the
    25	tree stands, every "this `V` is dead" fact is about an atlas the assembly does not use, and
    26	nothing says whether the interval is constrained at all for the real one.  **This file settles
    27	that**, and the answer is that the no-go does *not* propagate — with the obstruction isolated as
    28	a named hypothesis rather than left as a caveat.
    29	
    30	## What the multi-index argument actually proves
    31	
    32	Run the one-chart proof at a general family.  Coverage at the test `X i₀`, the tautological
    33	section of `f i₀`, and a point `t ∉ V i₀` returns `W ∋ t`, an index `i`, and
    34	`x : ↥W ⟶ ↥(V i)` with
    35	
    36	```
    37	(f i).app (op ↥W) (x ≫ (V i).ι)  =  (f i₀).app (op ↥W) (W.ι)
    38	```
    39	
    40	Two *different* points of the disjoint union of the chart sources therefore carry the same
    41	value.  That is `¬ JointlyInjective f`, and it is all the argument gives: joint injectivity is
    42	the conjunction of index separation and per-chart injectivity
    43	(`jointlyInjective_iff`), and only the second half is what the one-chart theorem concluded.
    44	
    45	## The premise that would restore the no-go, and the trap in stating it
    46	
    47	Recovering the one-chart conclusion needs a premise ruling out the crossing case.  The obvious
    48	one is "distinct indices never share a value", and **stating it over all tests makes it
    49	vacuous**: `IndexSeparatedAll` is equivalent to `Subsingleton ι` for *every* family
    50	(`indexSeparatedAll_iff_subsingleton`), because the Σ-sheaf is a subsingleton at an empty test
    51	(`pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty`) and each `X i` supplies one via its `⊥` open.  A
    52	refutation of that condition is a fact about `ι`, not about the charts — which is why it is
    53	landed here as a theorem, so nobody re-states it.
    54	
    55	`IndexSeparated` is the repair: the same condition **at tests that have a point**.  That is the
    56	form the coverage argument consumes anyway (the test it produces contains the point it started
    57	from), and it is a genuine hypothesis about `f`: `not_indexSeparated_duplicated` refutes it at a
    58	two-chart family whose every member *is* injective (`injective_duplicated`), on the test
    59	`Spec k`, which has a point.  So per-chart injectivity — all the one-chart no-go concludes —
    60	does not deliver it, and a glueing atlas, whose charts overlap by construction, is the shape
    61	that evades the no-go.
    62	
    63	The positive form is `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_indexSeparated_of_ne_top`: coverage
    64	at a proper `V i₀` *plus* index separation refutes injectivity of that chart.  Whether that
    65	premise holds for the Abel atlas at `|ι| ≥ 2` is **not measured here**, so the theorems
    66	conditioned on it are implications and not results about the seam; the second half of this file
    67	is the route that does not need it.
    68	
    69	## The honest limits
    70	
    71	* **Nothing here discharges an antecedent.**  `PointwiseCoverage` at a proper `V` has no
    72	  producer, and neither does its negation; every theorem below is an implication between open
    73	  propositions, or a statement about a concrete witness family.  What changes is that the
    74	  `V`-interval no-go is now known **not** to transmit to `mixedParamChart` through any premise
    75	  stated here except a point-independent witness index, so a lane may aim antecedent 1 at a
    76	  genuinely large `ι` without the landed refutations standing in its way.
    77	* **This is not a claim that the multi-index seam is satisfiable.**  Refuting a refutation is
    78	  not an inhabitation.  `(huniv V, hcov V)` remains unmeasured at every `V`, at every `ι`.
    79	* **Everything is stated for an arbitrary family of big-site presheaf maps.**  No divisor
    80	  scheme, chart index, twist, `rep` or `pic⁰` fact enters any statement or proof, exactly as in
    81	  the one-chart file — so nothing here depends on which atlas a producer eventually builds.
    82	* **`IndexSeparated` and `JointlyInjective` are restricted to NONEMPTY tests, and that is
    83	  load-bearing rather than cosmetic.**  An earlier version of this file quantified them over all
    84	  tests; a fresh-context audit found that version equivalent to `Subsingleton ι`, so its
    85	  refutation was a fact about the index type and the headline read backwards.  The unrestricted
    86	  form is retained as `IndexSeparatedAll` with `indexSeparatedAll_iff_subsingleton` as its
    87	  epitaph.  Any further predicate on this Σ-sheaf should be probed at the empty test before its
    88	  refutation is called a finding.
    89	* **`IndexSeparated` IS satisfiable at two distinct indices** (`indexSeparated_satFam`,
    90	  `not_subsingleton_ulift_bool`), so the repair is not a slower vacuity.  But the witness uses an
    91	  **empty** chart source, which no producer would build, so satisfiability *at the Abel atlas*
    92	  remains open and the theorems conditioned on index separation are implications rather than
    93	  measurements of the seam.  `jointlyInjective_singleSpecFamily` inhabits `JointlyInjective` only
    94	  at `PUnit`.
    95	
    96	## Main declarations
    97	
    98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JointlyInjective` — the multi-index strengthening of per-test injectivity
    99	  at nonempty tests: the chart sources inject *jointly* into the Σ-sheaf.
   100	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IndexSeparated` — distinct indices never share a value on a test with a
   101	  point.
   102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jointlyInjective_iff` — joint injectivity **is** index separation plus
   103	  per-chart injectivity.  This is the decomposition that shows what the one-chart conclusion was.
   104	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_jointlyInjective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — **the multi-index
   105	  step**: coverage at a proper `V i₀` refutes joint injectivity, at arbitrary `ι`.
   106	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_indexSeparated_of_ne_top` — the
   107	  one-chart conclusion recovered at arbitrary `ι`, with the missing hypothesis explicit.
   108	* `AlgebraicGeometry.indexSeparated_of_subsingleton` — why the one-chart theorem needed none.
   109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_indexSeparated_duplicated` and
   110	  `AlgebraicGeometry.injective_duplicated` — the negative answer: an all-injective family that
   111	  is not index separated, so the added hypothesis is not free and the no-go does not propagate.
   112	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_crossing_or_not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` — the
   113	  dichotomy in the form a coverage lane consumes: the witness crossed to another chart, or the
   114	  tested chart is non-injective on the produced open.
   115	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_crossing_or_not_injective_mixedParamChart` and
   116	  `AlgebraicGeometry.not_pointwiseCoverage_mixedParamChart_of_jointlyInjective` — both
   117	  instantiated at `mixedParamChart`, i.e. at the atlas
   118	  `pic0RepresentableBy_of_restrictedChartFibre` actually takes, so the measurement is about the
   119	  real assembly and not about a one-chart stand-in.
   120	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jointlyInjective_singleSpecFamily` — the non-vacuity check: joint
   121	  injectivity is inhabited, so the refutation above is about the *index* and not about the
   122	  Σ-sheaf admitting no injective family at all.
   123	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IndexSeparatedAll` and
   124	  `AlgebraicGeometry.indexSeparatedAll_iff_subsingleton` — the naive index-separation condition
   125	  and **its vacuity**: over all tests it *is* `Subsingleton ι`, for every family.  Landed so the
   126	  trap is a theorem instead of a warning.
   127	* `AlgebraicGeometry.indexSeparated_satFam` with `AlgebraicGeometry.not_subsingleton_ulift_bool` —
   128	  the nonempty-test form **is** satisfiable at two distinct indices, so the repair above is not a

   130	* `AlgebraicGeometry.UniformCoverage` and
   131	  `AlgebraicGeometry.not_injective_of_uniformCoverage_of_ne_top` — the half needing no unmeasured

   133	  This is the landed one-chart theorem with `Subsingleton ι` replaced by a hypothesis naming the

   153	/-! ## The two multi-index injectivity notions -/
   154	
   155	variable (C) in
   156	/-- **The naive index-separation condition, kept only to be refuted**: distinct indices never
   157	share a value, quantified over *every* test including the empty one.
   158	
   159	This is the shape a lane reaches for first, and it is **vacuous**:
   160	`indexSeparatedAll_iff_subsingleton` proves it equivalent to `Subsingleton ι` for every family
   161	whatsoever.  It mentions `f` and does not constrain it — the empty test alone decides it, because
   162	the Σ-sheaf is a subsingleton there (`pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty`) and each `X i`
   163	supplies an empty test via its `⊥` open.
   164	
   165	It is defined here rather than avoided so the refutation is a theorem in Lean and not a warning
   166	in prose. -/
   167	def IndexSeparatedAll {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   168	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
   169	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ) (i j : ι) (x : (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj S)
   170	    (y : (yoneda.obj (X j)).obj S), (f i).app S x = (f j).app S y → i = j
   171	
   172	variable (C) in
   173	/-- **THE NAIVE CONDITION IS VACUOUS**: `IndexSeparatedAll f` is `Subsingleton ι`, for an
   174	arbitrary family of maps into the Σ-sheaf.
   175	
   176	Forward: instantiate at the empty test `↥(⊥ : (X i).Opens)`, where the unique maps out of the
   177	initial object have equal value because the Σ-sheaf's value there is a subsingleton
   178	(`pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty`, `Pic0ChartRestrictedFibreSat.lean:160`).  Backward is
   179	`Subsingleton.elim`.
   180	
   181	So a "distinct indices never share a value" hypothesis quantified over all tests says nothing
   182	about the chart maps at all, and refuting it at some family is not a fact about that family.
   183	`IndexSeparated` below is the repair: the same condition at tests that have a point. -/
   184	theorem indexSeparatedAll_iff_subsingleton {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   185	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
   186	    IndexSeparatedAll C f ↔ Subsingleton ι := by
   187	  constructor
   188	  · intro h
   189	    refine ⟨fun i j => ?_⟩
   190	    refine h (op ((⊥ : (X i).Opens) : Scheme.{u})) i j
   191	      (isInitialOfIsEmpty.to _) (isInitialOfIsEmpty.to _) ?_
   192	    exact (pic0Sigma_obj_subsingleton_of_isEmpty (C := C)
   193	      ((⊥ : (X i).Opens) : Scheme.{u})).elim _ _
   194	  · intro _ _ i j _ _ _
   195	    exact Subsingleton.elim i j
   196	
   197	variable (C) in
   198	/-- **Index separation, at tests that have a point**: two charts with different indices never
   199	take the same value on a *nonempty* test.
   200	
   201	The nonemptiness restriction is what makes this a hypothesis about `f` rather than about `ι`:
   202	without it the condition collapses to `Subsingleton ι`
   203	(`indexSeparatedAll_iff_subsingleton`), and with it an overlapping family genuinely refutes it
   204	(`not_indexSeparated_duplicated`).  It is also exactly the form the coverage argument consumes,
   205	since the test the argument produces contains the point it started from.
   206	
   207	This is the half of joint injectivity that has no one-chart counterpart, and the content of the
   208	gap between the one-chart no-go and the multi-index case. -/
   209	def IndexSeparated {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   210	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
   211	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : Nonempty S) (i j : ι) (x : (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj (op S))
   212	    (y : (yoneda.obj (X j)).obj (op S)),
   213	    (f i).app (op S) x = (f j).app (op S) y → i = j
   214	
   215	variable (C) in
   216	/-- **Joint injectivity of a chart family**: over every nonempty test, the disjoint union of the
   217	chart sources injects into the Σ-sheaf.
   218	
   219	For a one-element family this is per-test injectivity of the single chart map; for a general
   220	family it is strictly stronger (`jointlyInjective_iff`, `not_indexSeparated_duplicated`), and it
   221	is exactly the statement the multi-index coverage argument refutes.
   222	
   223	Restricted to nonempty tests for the same reason as `IndexSeparated`: at an empty test the
   224	Σ-sheaf is a subsingleton, so the unrestricted version would carry `Subsingleton ι` as a free
   225	consequence and say nothing about `f`. -/
   226	def JointlyInjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   227	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) : Prop :=
   228	  ∀ (S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : Nonempty S) (i j : ι) (x : (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj (op S))
   229	    (y : (yoneda.obj (X j)).obj (op S)),
   230	    (f i).app (op S) x = (f j).app (op S) y →
   231	      (⟨i, x⟩ : Σ i, (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj (op S)) = ⟨j, y⟩
   232	
   233	/-- **Joint injectivity decomposes**: it is index separation together with per-chart
   234	injectivity on every test.
   235	
   236	Read left to right this says what the multi-index coverage argument's conclusion contains; read
   237	right to left it says the one-chart theorem's conclusion (per-chart injectivity) is only *half*
   238	of what would be needed to run the refutation at a general `ι`. -/
   239	theorem jointlyInjective_iff {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   240	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
   241	    JointlyInjective C f ↔
   242	      IndexSeparated C f ∧ ∀ (i : ι) (S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : Nonempty S),
   243	        Function.Injective ((f i).app (op S)) := by
   244	  constructor
   245	  · intro h
   246	    refine ⟨fun S hS i j x y hxy => ?_, fun i S hS x y hxy => ?_⟩
   247	    · exact congrArg Sigma.fst (h S hS i j x y hxy)
   248	    · exact eq_of_heq (Sigma.mk.injEq .. ▸ h S hS i i x y hxy).2
   249	  · rintro ⟨hsep, hinj⟩ S hS i j x y hxy
   250	    obtain rfl : i = j := hsep S hS i j x y hxy
   251	    exact congrArg (fun z => (⟨i, z⟩ : Σ i, (yoneda.obj (X i)).obj (op S))) (hinj i S hS hxy)
   252	
   253	/-- Joint injectivity implies per-chart injectivity at nonempty tests — the direction a lane
   254	will reach for. -/
   255	theorem injective_of_jointlyInjective {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   256	    {f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (h : JointlyInjective C f)
   257	    (i : ι) (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : Nonempty S) : Function.Injective ((f i).app (op S)) :=
   258	  ((jointlyInjective_iff f).mp h).2 i S hS
   259	
   260	/-- **Index separation is free for a one-chart atlas** — the reason
   261	`not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top` needed no such hypothesis, and the reason its
   262	proof cannot be read as covering the general case.
   263	
   264	Note this is the *only* route to `IndexSeparated` that costs nothing: unlike the naive
   265	`IndexSeparatedAll`, which is `Subsingleton ι` outright, the nonempty-test form is not implied
   266	by a subsingleton-free hypothesis anywhere in this file. -/
   267	theorem indexSeparated_of_subsingleton {ι : Type u} [Subsingleton ι] {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   268	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) :
   269	    IndexSeparated C f :=
   270	  fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ => Subsingleton.elim _ _
   271	
   272	/-! ## The multi-index step -/
   273	
   274	variable (C) in
   275	/-- **COVERAGE AT A PROPER `V i₀` REFUTES JOINT INJECTIVITY, AT ARBITRARY `ι`.**
   276	
   277	The one-chart argument of `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top`, run at a general
   278	family: the tautological section of `f i₀`, tested at `X i₀` and read at a point outside
   279	`V i₀`, is matched by a coverage witness that factors through `V i` for *some* index `i`.  Those
   280	are two different points of the disjoint union of the chart sources with the same value.
   281	
   282	The conclusion is about the family, not about `f i₀`: that is exactly the loss the one-chart
   283	file predicted, made precise.  Nothing beyond the equation is used — no divisor, chart index,
   284	twist, `rep`, or `pic⁰` fact. -/
   285	theorem not_jointlyInjective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   286	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
   287	    (i₀ : ι) (hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤)
   288	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
   289	    ¬ JointlyInjective C f := by
   290	  intro h
   291	  obtain ⟨hsep, hinj⟩ := (jointlyInjective_iff f).mp h
   292	  -- `V i₀ ≠ ⊤` gives a point of `X i₀` outside `V i₀`
   293	  obtain ⟨t, htV⟩ : ∃ t : X i₀, t ∉ V i₀ := by
   294	    by_contra hc
   295	    exact hV (top_le_iff.mp fun t _ => not_not.mp fun ht => hc ⟨t, ht⟩)
   296	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx⟩ := hcov (X i₀) ((f i₀).app (op (X i₀)) (𝟙 (X i₀))) t
   297	  -- the coverage witness at index `i` and the identity at index `i₀` agree over `W`
   298	  have hxv : (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (x ≫ (V i).ι)
   299	      = (f i₀).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (W.ι ≫ 𝟙 (X i₀)) := by
   300	    rw [← chart_map_ι_apply (f i₀) W (𝟙 (X i₀))]
   301	    exact hx
   302	  -- the produced test contains `t`, so it is nonempty: the hypotheses apply at it
   303	  have hWne : Nonempty (W : Scheme.{u}) := ⟨⟨t, htW⟩⟩
   304	  -- index separation collapses the two indices, and then per-chart injectivity the two points
   305	  obtain rfl : i = i₀ := hsep _ hWne i i₀ _ _ hxv
   306	  have heq := hinj i _ hWne hxv
   307	  -- but they disagree at `t`: the witness lands in `V i` and `t` does not
   308	  have hpt : ((x ≫ (V i).ι).base ⟨t, htW⟩ : X i)
   309	      = ((W.ι ≫ 𝟙 (X i)).base ⟨t, htW⟩ : X i) := by rw [heq]
   310	  have hmem : ((x ≫ (V i).ι).base ⟨t, htW⟩ : X i) ∈ V i := (x.base ⟨t, htW⟩).2
   311	  rw [hpt] at hmem
   312	  exact htV (by simpa using hmem)
   313	
   314	variable (C) in
   315	/-- **The one-chart conclusion, recovered at arbitrary `ι` with the missing hypothesis
   316	explicit**: coverage at a proper `V i₀` together with index separation refutes injectivity of
   317	the tested chart on some test.
   318	
   319	At `ι := PUnit` the index-separation hypothesis is free (`indexSeparated_of_subsingleton`), so
   320	this contains `not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top`; at a general `ι` it is a genuine
   321	extra premise, and `not_indexSeparated_duplicated` shows it is not one an overlapping atlas
   322	supplies. -/
   323	theorem not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_indexSeparated_of_ne_top
   324	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   325	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
   326	    (i₀ : ι) (hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤) (hsep : IndexSeparated C f)
   327	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
   328	    ∃ (i : ι) (S : Scheme.{u}) (_ : Nonempty S),
   329	      ¬ Function.Injective ((f i).app (op S)) := by
   330	  by_contra hall
   331	  simp only [not_exists, not_not] at hall
   332	  exact not_jointlyInjective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top C f V i₀ hV hcov
   333	    ((jointlyInjective_iff f).mpr ⟨hsep, fun i S hS => hall i S hS⟩)
   334	
   335	variable (C) in
   336	/-- **THE DICHOTOMY, WITH ITS WITNESS EXHIBITED** — the form a coverage lane consumes.
   337	
   338	Coverage at a proper `V i₀` produces an open `W` of `X i₀` and an index `i` such that a
   339	`W`-point of `X i` and the inclusion `W.ι` carry the same class, and then **either** `i ≠ i₀`
   340	(the coverage witness crossed to another chart) **or** `f i₀` is non-injective on `W`.
   341	
   342	This is the actionable content of the multi-index measurement.  The one-chart theorem is the
   343	case where the first alternative is unavailable, so it reads off the second; at a general `ι`
   344	a lane supplying coverage must say which alternative its witness realises, and
   345	`not_indexSeparated_duplicated` shows nothing in the shape of an overlapping atlas forces the
   346	second.  Both alternatives are about the *family*, so neither can be dismissed by a fact about
   347	one chart. -/
   348	theorem exists_crossing_or_not_injective_of_pointwiseCoverage_of_ne_top
   349	    {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   350	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1) (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
   351	    (i₀ : ι) (hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤)
   352	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (fun i => restrictChart (f i) (V i))) :
   353	    ∃ (W : (X i₀).Opens) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   354	      (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x
   355	          = (f i₀).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (W.ι) ∧
   356	        (i ≠ i₀ ∨ ¬ Function.Injective ((f i₀).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})))) := by
   357	  classical
   358	  obtain ⟨t, htV⟩ : ∃ t : X i₀, t ∉ V i₀ := by
   359	    by_contra hc
   360	    exact hV (top_le_iff.mp fun t _ => not_not.mp fun ht => hc ⟨t, ht⟩)
   361	  obtain ⟨W, htW, i, x, hx⟩ := hcov (X i₀) ((f i₀).app (op (X i₀)) (𝟙 (X i₀))) t
   362	  have hxv : (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (x ≫ (V i).ι)
   363	      = (f i₀).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) (W.ι) := by
   364	    rw [show (W.ι : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i₀) = W.ι ≫ 𝟙 (X i₀) from (Category.comp_id _).symm,
   365	      ← chart_map_ι_apply (f i₀) W (𝟙 (X i₀))]
   366	    exact hx
   367	  refine ⟨W, i, x ≫ (V i).ι, hxv, ?_⟩
   368	  by_cases hi : i = i₀
   369	  · subst hi
   370	    -- same index: the two points differ at `t`, so the chart is not injective there
   371	    refine Or.inr fun hinj => ?_
   372	    have heq := hinj hxv
   373	    have hmem : ((x ≫ (V i).ι).base ⟨t, htW⟩ : X i) ∈ V i := (x.base ⟨t, htW⟩).2
   374	    rw [show ((x ≫ (V i).ι).base ⟨t, htW⟩ : X i) = (W.ι.base ⟨t, htW⟩ : X i) from by rw [heq]]
   375	      at hmem
   376	    exact htV (by simpa using hmem)
   377	  · exact Or.inl hi

   380	family all of whose charts are injective admits coverage at no proper `V`. -/
   381	theorem not_pointwiseCoverage_of_jointlyInjective_of_ne_top {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   382	    {f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1} (V : ∀ i, (X i).Opens)
   383	    (i₀ : ι) (hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤) (hinj : JointlyInjective C f) :

   387	/-! ## The composition at the atlas the seam actually consumes

   397	/-- **The dichotomy at `mixedParamChart`**, i.e. at the real atlas.
   398	
   399	`mixedParamChart` is `restrictChart` of `abelSigmaChart` applied pointwise, so the coverage

   408	theorem exists_crossing_or_not_injective_mixedParamChart {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)

   410	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))

   425	    (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) V i₀ hV hcov

   427	variable (C π) in
   428	/-- **The positive branch at the real atlas**: an index-separated Abel atlas all of whose charts
   429	are injective supports coverage at no proper `V i₀`.
   430	
   431	At `ι := PUnit` this is `not_pointwiseCoverage_of_injective_of_ne_top`
   432	(`Pic0ChartCoverForcesNonInj.lean`), whose index-separation premise is free there.  At the real
   433	`ι` the premise is an extra obligation on the atlas, and the point of this file is that no

   435	theorem not_pointwiseCoverage_mixedParamChart_of_jointlyInjective {ι : Type u} (nn : ι → ℕ)
   436	    (D : ι → Over (Spec (.of k)))
   437	    (rep : ∀ i, (divFunctor C π (nn i)).RepresentableBy (D i))
   438	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   439	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   440	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (nn i : ℤ))
   441	    (V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens) (i₀ : ι) (hV : V i₀ ≠ ⊤)
   442	    (hinj : JointlyInjective C
   443	      (fun i => abelSigmaChart C π (nn i) (rep i) (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i))) :
   444	    ¬ PointwiseCoverage C (mixedParamChart C π nn D rep m Z hdeg V) :=
   445	  not_pointwiseCoverage_of_jointlyInjective_of_ne_top V i₀ hV hinj

   447	/-! ## The second way to close the crossing alternative: a uniform index
   448	
   449	Index separation is one way to rule out the crossing alternative, and
   450	`not_indexSeparated_duplicated` shows an overlapping atlas does not supply it.  There is a
   451	second, and it is the one a coverage lane can actually produce: coverage that always returns
   452	*the same* index.  That is what a chart whose locus is the whole test gives, so this section is
   453	the joint with the coverage side rather than with the injectivity side. -/
